title: What will this meeting decide?

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: that an agenda item needs the intended outcome and who decides, or the meeting can end without a decision

misconception: A topic on the agenda implies a decision and a decider.
objective: Add a desired outcome and decision owner to an agenda.

claims.text: Scenario and prediction: The agenda item reads 'Topic: plan'. With only 'Topic: plan' on the agenda, who decides what? Correct option: The agenda doesn't say. All fixture labels, example words and names are stipulated exercise data.
claims.source: Stipulated exercise fixture in studyCatalog.ts. Content patch r9 batch D (cm-lifehacks, company/reviews/lifehacks-200/content-patch-r9-batch-d.md block 6), applied by demo-builder for W-608 (2026-10-14).
claims.note: FC W-740 (2026-10-14): Fixture: one topic field filled, outcome and owner empty in mode A; the stage names no decider, so "The agenda doesn't say" is the only option the page supports. Stipulated data.

claims.text: The agenda’s checklist requires topic, outcome and decision owner. It records what the meeting is meant to produce, not whether the meeting will be effective.

claims.text: Only 'picks' names the choice the meeting must end with and who makes it. Presenting or discussing names a topic and a person, not a decision.

claims.text: A topic-only agenda tells the room the topic only; with outcome and owner added, it names the choice and who decides (Bo).
